checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are accurate and rigorous. It correctly identified that while the object has the general silhouette of a sign (circular panel on a post), it fails almost all functional and material checkpoints. Specifically, the lack of legible text/symbols (Functional) and the absence of mounting hardware (Geometry) are critical failures. The Router was not too lenient; in fact, marking 'High-contrast coloration' as present is generous but technically true regarding pixel values, even if semantically useless.
artifact_review: The Router correctly identified 'text_gibberish' as a severity 5 artifact. This is the defining defect of the image. The 'structural_collapse' (severity 3) at the edges is also well-noted; the white shapes bleed into the red background in a way that defies physical printing processes. The 'perspective_distortion' (severity 2) is subtle but present in the rim thickness. The Reflector agrees with these severities. The Perceptual Quality Auditor missed the semantic distortion because it only looks for noise/blur, but the Router's visual inspection correctly caught the structural/textual artifacts.
alignment_reasoning: The image receives a very low alignment score. While the Fine Grained Classifier did predict 'street sign' (likely due to the circular shape and red color resembling a Stop sign), the object fails the taxonomy definition which requires 'text, symbols, or pictograms for public navigation'. The gibberish markings do not constitute valid symbols. Only the basic geometry (panel on post) and contrast align with the class. 2/9 checkpoints passed.
artifact_reasoning: The artifact score is low (poor quality) primarily due to the catastrophic text rendering (Severity 5). The characters are melted, nonsensical, and structurally impossible. Additionally, the boundary between the graphics and the sign face shows fusion/bleeding artifacts (Severity 3), and the sign rim exhibits inconsistent perspective warping (Severity 2). These are definitive AI generation errors.
